definitions.explanation: The start of the fiscal or academic year in Japan, which falls on April 1st. A period of significant transitions including new school terms, new hires, and organizational changes.

examples.japanese: {年度始|ねんどはじ}めは{忙|いそが}しい。
examples.english: The beginning of the fiscal year is busy.

examples.japanese: {年度始|ねんどはじ}めに{新|あたら}しい{制度|せいど}が{始|はじ}まる。
examples.english: A new system starts at the beginning of the fiscal year.

examples.japanese: {年度始|ねんどはじ}めは{人事異動|じんじいどう}や{入社式|にゅうしゃしき}があり、{会社|かいしゃ}は{慌|あわ}ただしい。
examples.english: The start of the fiscal year is hectic with personnel transfers and new employee ceremonies.

notes:
In Japan, the fiscal and academic year begins on April 1st. This is a major transition point: students enter new school years, new employees start work, and government budgets reset.

RELATED TERMS:
- {年度末|ねんどまつ} — end of the fiscal year (March)
- {年度|ねんど} — fiscal year
- {新年度|しんねんど} — new fiscal year
- {会計年度|かいけいねんど} — accounting fiscal year

{年度始|ねんどはじ}め events include {入学式|にゅうがくしき} (entrance ceremonies), {入社式|にゅうしゃしき} (new employee ceremonies), and {人事異動|じんじいどう} (personnel transfers).
